newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says it busts big international drug ring.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says it busts big international drug ring.

text.p: U.S. officials said police arrested 34 people in Thailand, Pakistan and the United States on Friday, breaking up an operation run mainly by Nigerian women that smuggled heroin into the United States.

"Earlier this morning more than 100 federal and local law enforcement officers dismantled an alleged international heroin-smuggling ring. They arrested 34 of its members at five locations around the world, including Bangkok, Pakistan, New York, Chicago and Detroit," Attorney General Janet Reno told a news conference.
The operation, code-named "Global Sea," involved what Reno described as unprecedented cooperation of law enforcement officials in Thailand, France and Great Britain with U.S. authorities.
U.S. officials said they seized more than 55 kg (121 lb) of heroin with an estimated total retail value exceeding $26 million.

Drug Enforcement Administration chief Thomas Constantine said the case marked the first time so many women had been involved in a drug smuggling ring, rising to a leadership position while also serving as couriers.

U.S. officials said the heroin originated in Thailand and Cambodia. Under one route, it was shipped directly to Boston while the other route involved transporting it through Paris or Amsterdam, to Guatemala, into Mexico and then to Chicago.
